name: Asylum -- Refugee and Humanitarian/Subsidiary Protection Status (Law No. 270-XVI of 2008)

qualifying_event.description: Moldova is a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention and its 1967 Protocol and operates a genuine domestic asylum system under Law No. 270-XVI of 18.12.2008, administered by the Bureau for Migration and Asylum (BMA). An eligibility-counsellor interview determines status; rejections are appealable, though the exact appeal mechanism/timeframe was not confirmed in this build.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Evidence supporting a well-founded fear of persecution per Convention grounds.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution on Convention grounds (race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership of a particular social group), assessed by the Bureau for Migration and Asylum.

outcome.duration_length: not confirmed in this build -- open gap on the specific permit validity period

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR-hosted) -- unofficial translation of Law No. 270-XVI of 18.12.2008 on Asylum in the Republic of Moldova

Bureau for Migration and Asylum (legacy igm.gov.md domain) -- rights and duties of asylum seekers/refugees: work (employment, self-employment, professions), freedom of movement/residence, compulsory education access on par with citizens, social assistance for families with children, medical insurance parity, court access

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Moldova). STATUS: DRAFT -- the hard requirement (meeting the Refugee Convention definition) is sourced to a tier-2 UNHCR-hosted translation of the primary law, since BMA's own procedural page (bma.gov.md 'Solicitarea azilului') returned a fetch error in this build; only the companion tier-1 rights-and-duties page loaded successfully, which is why work/study/family rights are tier-1 confirmed even though the file overall stays draft. STRUCTURAL FINDING: unlike Qatar (narrow political-asylum-only law, no Convention signature) or the UNHCR-mandate pattern seen in Jordan/Mongolia/Cote d'Ivoire built elsewhere in this dataset, Moldova runs a GENUINE Convention-based domestic asylum system with its own administering authority (BMA). GAP: the specific appeal mechanism/timeframe and the exact permit-validity period were not confirmed. pr_after_months (60) and citizenship_after_months (96, the reduced 8-year track) are cross-referenced from md_permanent_residence.json and md_citizenship_naturalisation.json's reduced-period group respectively, not independently sourced here. This file is distinct from md_temporary_protection.json, which covers Moldova's separate, currently active EU-aligned temporary protection scheme for people displaced from Ukraine.
